_comment: Scenario battery for Plantar Fascia Clinic's node_6a fork (claude-haiku-4-5, Override: Disabled). This clinic forks the shared node_6a only in EXECUTE's success handling (SUPPORT PERSON FOLLOW-UP + prep-video promise). 2026-08-18: gated the bring-someone question and prep-video promise on {{appointment_type_id}}=='2010559925616385733' (Initial Consultation) — previously unconditional, which told returning patients booking a Subsequent Consultation (id 2010560230416457414) 'before your first session...' and promised a video/email the backend never sends for a non-initial appointment_type (see tools/sms_manager.py's is_initial_appointment gate, tools/booking_stages/side_effects.py's _resolve_is_initial). Tagged 'initial-vs-followup-video-gate' for this fix.

scenarios.name: PFC1 — Initial Consultation success asks bring-someone question

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" appointment_type="Initial Consultation" patient_name="Sam Rivera" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee."}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks the message verbatim then, same turn, as a separate sentence, asks 'Before your first session it is very helpful if you can bring someone with you to help your recovery. Do you have anyone you could bring?' and waits — no tool call this turn. FAIL if the question is skipped, blended into the message, or a tool is called this turn.

scenarios.name: PFC2 — Initial Consultation follow-up (affirmative) speaks video promise and wraps up

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.
smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee."}
You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee. Before your first session it is very helpful if you can bring someone with you to help your recovery. Do you have anyone you could bring?
Yeah, my partner can come.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent says 'Great, one more thing before we wrap up the call.' then, same turn, speaks the prep-video promise verbatim ('You will receive a text message and email that will give you access to our pre appointment preparation videos and information. We highly recommend you watch these to get the most out your first session.') then calls universal_router intent='wrap_up' — all in one turn. FAIL if the video promise or wrap_up call is missing or split across turns.

scenarios.name: PFC3 — Initial Consultation follow-up (negative) still speaks video promise and wraps up

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.
smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Monday at 9am with Dr. Lee."}
You're all booked in for Monday at 9am with Dr. Lee. Before your first session it is very helpful if you can bring someone with you to help your recovery. Do you have anyone you could bring?
No, I don't think so.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent says 'That's ok, one more thing before we wrap up the call.' then, same turn, speaks the prep-video promise verbatim then calls universal_router intent='wrap_up' — all in one turn. A negative reply must still get the video promise, same as an affirmative reply.

scenarios.name: PFC4 — Subsequent Consultation success skips bring-someone question and video promise entirely

history.content: Yes that's right, go ahead.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010560230416457414" appointment_type="Subsequent Consultation" patient_name="Jordan Blake" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee."}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks the message verbatim, does NOT ask the bring-someone question, does NOT mention 'first session' or any prep-video/text/email promise, and in the SAME turn calls universal_router intent='wrap_up'. FAIL if the bring-someone question or video promise appears anywhere for this booking.

scenarios.name: PFC5 — Caller speaks again after Subsequent-Consultation wrap_up (regression, no dangling follow-up)

history.content: Yes that's right, go ahead.
Checking that now, one moment.
smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010560230416457414" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee."}
You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee.
Oh wait, actually can you tell me the address?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent answers the address question normally (ADDRESS INLINE / INFO PIVOT per the system prompt) without getting stuck waiting on a bring-someone reply or trying to speak a video promise — none was ever started for this Subsequent Consultation booking.

scenarios.name: PFC-NC1 — Name correction instead of bring-someone answer (SUPPORT PERSON FOLLOW-UP / name-correction interaction)

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" appointment_type="Initial Consultation" patient_name="Sarah Jones" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee."}
You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee. Before your first session it is very helpful if you can bring someone with you to help your recovery. Do you have anyone you could bring?
No wait, actually my name's Theresa, not Sarah.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent recognizes this as a name correction, not a decline to the bring-someone question — does NOT say 'That's ok, one more thing...' and does NOT speak the video promise this turn. Instead applies the CONFIRM judgement to 'Theresa', then calls smart_voice_agent intent='update_contact_detail' with field='first_name', value='Theresa'. FAIL if the reply is misread as a negative answer to the bring-someone question and the SUPPORT PERSON FOLLOW-UP / video-promise / wrap_up path fires instead, silently dropping the correction.

scenarios.name: PFC-NC2 — Name correction after a Subsequent Consultation booking (no support-person question ever asked)

history.content: Yes that's right, go ahead.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010560230416457414" appointment_type="Subsequent Consultation" patient_name="Jordan Blake" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee."}
You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee.
Oh wait, actually you have my name wrong — it's Blaike, not Blake.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent applies the CONFIRM spelling judgement to the corrected last name, then calls smart_voice_agent intent='update_contact_detail' with field='last_name', value='Blaike'. FAIL if the correction is routed to plain wrap_up with no tool call — this Subsequent Consultation booking never triggered a bring-someone question, so SUPPORT PERSON FOLLOW-UP's gate should never apply here either.

scenarios.name: PFC-NC3 — Full-name correction after support-person question already answered normally (one call, not two)

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.
smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" patient_name="Sarah Jones" -> {"success": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee."}
You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee. Before your first session it is very helpful if you can bring someone with you to help your recovery. Do you have anyone you could bring?
No, not really.

That's ok, one more thing before we wrap up the call. You will receive a text message and email that will give you access to our pre appointment preparation videos and information. We highly recommend you watch these to get the most out your first session.
universal_router intent="wrap_up" -> {"message": ""}
Wait, actually — my full name is Theresa Nguyen, not Sarah Jones.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent calls smart_voice_agent intent='update_contact_detail' with field='full_name', value='Theresa Nguyen' — a single call covering both name parts, never two separate calls for first/last.

scenarios.name: RC1 — Email single-character correction escalates to anchor word

history.content: Hi, I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Chris Fielding
So that's Chris Fielding — is that right?
Yes.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Yep — csmith81 at outlook dot com
So that's C, S, M, I, T, H, eight, one, at outlook dot com — is that right?
No, it's an S not a C — s-smith81.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the correction confirmation pairs the corrected letter with a short disambiguating word (e.g. "an S, as in Sam, instead of a C, as in Charlie" or an equivalent anchor-word phrasing for S and C) rather than repeating bare letters. FAIL if the readback says only "an S instead of a C" with no anchor word — this is a retry after the first bare-letter readback already needed correcting, so RE-CONFIRMATION ESCALATION applies.

scenarios.name: RC2 — Full email restate after failed confirmation escalates to anchor-word read-back

history.content: Hi, I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Marcus Webb
So that's Marcus Webb — is that right?
Yes.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Yeah — benfield19 at bigpond dot com
So that's B, E, N, F, I, E, L, D, one, nine, at bigpond dot com — is that right?
No that's not right at all — it's D-E-N-F-I-E-L-D, denfield19, at bigpond dot com

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if the agent treats this as a fresh full restate (not a partial merge with the old spelling) and reads the entire local part back letter-by-letter pairing each letter with a short anchor word (e.g. "D as in Delta, E as in Echo..."), not bare uppercase letters. Clustering the letters into short groups is a bonus, not required for PASS. FAIL if the re-confirmation uses bare letters identical in form to the first (already-wrong) attempt.

scenarios.name: RC3 — Last-name re-spell after a failed CONFIRM escalates to anchor words

history.content: Hi, I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Anthony Nguyen
And could you spell your last name for me?
N, G, U, Y, E, N
So that's N, G, U, Y, E, N — is that right?
No, that's not quite it.
Sorry — could you spell it again for me?
N, G, U, Y, E, N

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if this second readback of the surname pairs each letter with a disambiguating word (e.g. "N as in November, G as in Golf...") since the first plain readback already didn't land. FAIL if this second readback repeats bare uppercase letters identical in form to the first attempt.

scenarios.name: EAM1 — Ambiguous plain "no" after email confirm: agent asks which half was wrong instead of assuming the local part

history.content: I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Priya Nair
So that's Priya Nair — is that right?
Yes.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Yeah.
What is it?
priya at fernwoodclinic dot com
So that's priya at fernwoodclinic dot com — is that right?
No.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent asks a disambiguating question naming both halves — e.g. 'Sorry — was it the part before the @ or the domain that wasn't right?' — since the caller's plain 'no' gave no delta to work from. FAIL if agent assumes the local part was wrong and asks the caller to spell it out (or otherwise targets one specific half) without first asking which half was wrong. FAIL if agent silently re-confirms the same unchanged address.

scenarios.name: EAM2 — Caller repeats the full email instead of a delta: agent reparses fresh and spells both halves back

history.content: I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Priya Nair
So that's Priya Nair — is that right?
Yes.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Yeah.
What is it?
hello at theadhdnaturopath dot com
So that's hello at theadhdnaturopath dot com — is that right?
No.
Sorry — was it the part before the @ or the domain that wasn't right?
Hello at theadhdnaturopath dot com.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent treats this as a fresh full statement rather than a partial correction, and spells the entire address back letter by letter for both the local part and the domain, using RE-CONFIRMATION ESCALATION's anchor-word form since this is a retry (e.g. 'So that's H as in Hotel, E as in Echo, L as in Lima, L as in Lima, O as in Oscar, at T as in Tango, H as in Hotel...'), not bare uppercase letters identical in form to the first attempt. Clustering the letters into short groups is a bonus, not required for PASS. FAIL if agent merges the restated email with only part of the previous one, spells back only the local part while leaving the domain in prose form, asks another open-ended 'what should it be' question instead of reparsing what was just said, or uses bare letters with no anchor words.

scenarios.name: EMS1 — text-me-instead asks MOBILE CHECK instead of executing immediately

history.content: Hi, I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Sarah Kowalski
So that's Sarah Kowalski — is that right?
Yes, that's right.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Can you just text me instead?

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent asks the MOBILE CHECK question ('Are you on your mobile right now? I can text you to grab that.' or a close variant) and does NOT call smart_voice_agent yet — the text-me-instead outcome now requires confirming the caller can receive the text before executing. FAIL if agent calls smart_voice_agent in this turn (with or without email_capture_requested) instead of asking MOBILE CHECK first. FAIL if agent calls send_details_to_caller.

scenarios.name: EMS1b — MOBILE CHECK confirmed sets email_capture_requested in EXECUTE payload

history.content: Hi, I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Sarah Kowalski
So that's Sarah Kowalski — is that right?
Yes, that's right.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Can you just text me instead?
Are you on your mobile right now? I can text you to grab that.
Yeah, I'm on it now.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks exactly 'Checking that now, one moment.' AND calls smart_voice_agent intent='book' with patient_email omitted AND email_capture_requested: true included in the payload (name confirmed, phone already known, email resolved via text-me-instead, MOBILE CHECK confirmed — EXECUTE fires this turn). FAIL if email_capture_requested is missing from the payload. FAIL if agent asks any further question instead of executing.

scenarios.name: EMS1c — MOBILE CHECK declined executes with no email and no email_capture_requested

history.content: Hi, I'd like to book an appointment.
What's your full name for the booking?
Sarah Kowalski
So that's Sarah Kowalski — is that right?
Yes, that's right.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
Can you just text me instead?
Are you on your mobile right now? I can text you to grab that.
No, I'm on the landline at reception.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks exactly 'Checking that now, one moment.' AND calls smart_voice_agent intent='book' with BOTH patient_email and email_capture_requested omitted entirely from the payload (caller declined the MOBILE CHECK — proceed to EXECUTE with no email at all, same as a plain decline, rather than promising a text that can't be delivered). FAIL if email_capture_requested is included with any value. FAIL if agent re-asks for an email address instead of executing.

scenarios.name: EMS2 — plain decline does NOT set email_capture_requested

history.content: I need to book in please.
What's your full name for the booking?
Tom Reilly
So that's Tom Reilly — is that right?
Yep.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
No, don't have one, thanks.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks exactly 'Checking that now, one moment.' AND calls smart_voice_agent intent='book' with BOTH patient_email and email_capture_requested omitted entirely from the payload — a plain decline is not the text-me-instead or skip-after-repeated-attempts outcome, so EMAIL-CAPTURE-VIA-SMS does not apply. FAIL if email_capture_requested is included (with any value) for this plain decline.

scenarios.name: EMS3 — skip-for-now agreement after repeated ambiguous replies asks MOBILE CHECK instead of executing immediately

history.content: Hi, can I book an appointment please.
What's your full name for the booking?
Priya Chandra
So that's Priya Chandra — is that right?
Yes.
Do you have an email address for the booking?
uh, what?
Do you have an email address for the booking?
sorry, come again?
No problem if you don't have one — shall I skip the email for now?
yeah let's just skip it

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent asks the MOBILE CHECK question ('Are you on your mobile right now? I can text you to grab that.' or a close variant) and does NOT call smart_voice_agent yet — two ambiguous replies triggered the skip offer and the caller agreed, but EMAIL-CAPTURE-VIA-SMS now requires confirming the caller can receive a text before executing (same gate as an explicit text-me-instead request — see EMS1/EMS1b/EMS1c). FAIL if agent calls smart_voice_agent in this turn instead of asking MOBILE CHECK first.

scenarios.name: PE1 — PHONE-SKIP + patient.email in availability tool result: email already known, EXECUTE fires without asking

history.content: TOOL RESULT (smart_voice_agent intent="availability"): {"success": true, "found": true, "patient": {"name": "George Norris", "email": "george.norris@yahoo.co.uk"}, "practitioners": [{"practitioner_name": "Mark Taylor", "dates": [{"date": "2026-08-13", "slot_groups": {"morning": ["9 AM"]}}]}]}
The 9 AM works for me.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks 'Checking that now, one moment.' AND calls smart_voice_agent intent='book' with patient_email='george.norris@yahoo.co.uk' — PHONE-SKIP fires (caller_first_name + caller_last_name set, caller_id non-empty), step 3's 'Already known' check finds patient.email='george.norris@yahoo.co.uk' in the tool result in conversation history, email treated as resolved, EXECUTE fires. FAIL if agent asks 'Do you have an email address for the booking?' (patient.email in tool result was ignored). FAIL if smart_voice_agent is called silently without the spoken filler phrase.

scenarios.name: KTR1 — KNOWN-CALLER FAST-PATH: caller_email DV empty but patient.email in tool result: EXECUTE fires without asking

history.content: TOOL RESULT (smart_voice_agent intent="availability"): {"success": true, "found": true, "patient": {"name": "George Norris", "email": "george.norris@yahoo.co.uk"}, "practitioners": [{"practitioner_name": "Mark Taylor", "dates": [{"date": "2026-08-13", "slot_groups": {"morning": ["9 AM"]}}]}]}
Yeah, go ahead and book me in.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks 'Checking that now, one moment.' AND calls smart_voice_agent intent='book' with patient_email='george.norris@yahoo.co.uk' — KNOWN-CALLER FAST-PATH fires because caller_first_name, caller_last_name, and caller_id are all set AND patient.email is present in the prior smart_voice_agent tool result in conversation history, even though caller_email DV is empty. FAIL if agent asks 'Do you have an email address for the booking?' (patient.email in tool result was not checked by KNOWN-CALLER FAST-PATH). FAIL if smart_voice_agent is called silently without the spoken phrase.

scenarios.name: WL1 — waitlist_offer_pending=true: speaks the waitlist question verbatim and HALTs, no bring-someone question this turn

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" appointment_type="Initial Consultation" patient_name="Sam Rivera" -> {"success": true, "waitlist_offer_pending": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee. Would you like me to also add you to the waitlist in case something sooner comes up?"}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks the message field verbatim with no additions (it already ends with the waitlist question) and then HALTs — no wrap_up call, and no bring-someone/prep-video question this turn even though this is an Initial Consultation. FAIL if agent adds the bring-someone question in the same turn (stacking two questions). FAIL if agent calls universal_router intent='wrap_up' this turn.

scenarios.name: WL2 — waitlist accepted on an Initial Consultation: waitlist_add called, then the bring-someone question follows (not wrap_up)

history.content: Yeah that's right, book me in.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010559925616385733" appointment_type="Initial Consultation" patient_name="Sam Rivera" -> {"success": true, "waitlist_offer_pending": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee. Would you like me to also add you to the waitlist in case something sooner comes up?"}
You're all booked in for Tuesday at 10am with Dr. Lee. Would you like me to also add you to the waitlist in case something sooner comes up?
Yes please, that'd be great.
Checking that now, one moment.
universal_router intent="waitlist_add" -> {"message": "You're on the waitlist — we'll call if something opens up sooner."}

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent speaks the waitlist_add result's message verbatim, then in the SAME turn asks 'Before your first session it is very helpful if you can bring someone with you to help your recovery. Do you have anyone you could bring?' and waits — no wrap_up call this turn (Initial Consultation still needs the bring-someone question, deferred while the waitlist question was pending). FAIL if agent calls universal_router intent='wrap_up' instead of asking the bring-someone question. FAIL if agent calls waitlist_add a second time.

scenarios.name: WL3 — waitlist declined on a Subsequent Consultation: no waitlist_add, straight to wrap_up

history.content: Yes that's right, go ahead.
Checking that now, one moment.

smart_voice_agent intent="book" appointment_type_id="2010560230416457414" appointment_type="Subsequent Consultation" patient_name="Jordan Blake" -> {"success": true, "waitlist_offer_pending": true, "message": "You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee. Would you like me to also add you to the waitlist in case something sooner comes up?"}
You're all booked in for Thursday at 2pm with Dr. Lee. Would you like me to also add you to the waitlist in case something sooner comes up?
No thanks, I'm good.

scenarios.expected_behavior: PASS if agent does NOT call waitlist_add and, in the same turn, calls universal_router intent='wrap_up' directly — this is a Subsequent Consultation, so no bring-someone question applies either way. FAIL if agent calls waitlist_add despite the decline. FAIL if agent asks the bring-someone question (wrong appointment type for it). FAIL if agent asks any further question instead of wrapping up.
